- Written argument: Invalid
- Statement: Refuted

- /probability_model: One probability space carries the triangular array {X_{n,j}}; every convergence-in-probability statement uses its measure P.

- /probability_model: The single probability space of Lemma 1 carries the array {X_{n,j}} and hence hat{theta}_n; convergence in probability uses its measure P.
- /hypotheses/0: The conditions of Lemma 1 hold: for each fixed j, X_{n,j} -> 0 in probability, and m_n -> infinity.
- /hypotheses/1: hat{theta}_n = theta_0 + max_{1 <= j <= m_n} |X_{n,j}|.

Support reasoning: The written implication is exact algebra conditional on the invoked maximum convergence, but that premise is unavailable. Independently, take m_n=n and X_{n,j}=1{j=n} on a one-point probability space. This directly refutes the exact claimed convergence, beyond merely identifying an unsupported dependency.

### I-001 [S1]: The proof promotes fixed-index convergence to a maximum over a growing range without valid uniform tail control. The lemma is refuted by the recorded Bernoulli array; an independently found deterministic moving-coordinate array also directly refutes the exact estimator theorem.

Finding: Defect; status: open; confidence: high; load-bearing: True.

Affected units: lem:growing-max, thm:main

Why the step fails:

Take X_{n,j} independent Bernoulli(1/n) and m_n = n^2: each fixed j has P(|X_{n,j}| > eps) = 1/n -> 0 when 0 < eps < 1, and zero when eps >= 1; also m_n -> infinity. Thus both hypotheses hold, whereas P(max_{1<=j<=m_n} |X_{n,j}| > 1/2) = 1 - (1 - 1/n)^{n^2} -> 1.

<a id="repair-b3219cf060fcaed7b2bc"></a>
Option 1: Add the hypothesis sup_{1<=j<=m_n} P(|X_{n,j}| > eps) <= a_n(eps) with m_n a_n(eps) -> 0 for every eps > 0, and derive line 16 from the union bound under it.
Scientific cost: the result statement changes; its downstream uses must be rechecked; stronger regularity or moment assumptions. Verification: candidate.
Required rechecks: lem:growing-max, thm:main

<a id="repair-7d576c7dad2854bd25b4"></a>
Option 2: Replace the growing range 1..m_n by a fixed finite range 1..K in the lemma and in every downstream use, so the finite union bound closes the step.
Scientific cost: the result statement changes; its downstream uses must be rechecked; no stronger assumption; the result applies in a narrower setting. Verification: candidate.
Required rechecks: lem:growing-max, thm:main

    \begin{lemma}\label{lem:growing-max}
    Let $\{X_{n,j} : 1 \le j \le m_n\}$ be random variables on one probability
    space such that $X_{n,j} \to 0$ in probability as $n \to \infty$ for each
    fixed $j$, and let $m_n \to \infty$. Then
    $\max_{1 \le j \le m_n} |X_{n,j}| \to 0$ in probability.
    \end{lemma}
